newsitem.title: POLAND: NUMBER OF POLISH BEER DRINKERS UP SIX PCT-POLL.
newsitem.headline: NUMBER OF POLISH BEER DRINKERS UP SIX PCT-POLL.

text.p: The number of Poles who drink beer has risen by six percent over the past year and half-way through the current year 64 percent of adults said they did, an annual survey by the Pentor agency showed on Tuesday.
"In comparison with the first half of 1996, a six percent rise in beer consumers was noted. It is drunk by 64 percent of Poles, while five percent drink it daily," Pentor official Maciej Kos said.
Kos told a news conference called to announce the results of the agency's seventh such annual report on beer consumption that the proportion of women beer lovers was rising steadily.

"Since 1994 the share of women in the structure of beer consumers has risen by four percent. Beer is still drunk mainly by men, who make up 60 percent of consumers and drink 74 percent of beer," Kos said.
He said 92 percent of drinkers favoured Polish-made brews.
"The best reviews from consumers were for Zywiec breweries (30 percent of those polled), Elblag (16 percent), Okocim (12 percent), Poznan (11 percent) and Tychy (six percent)," he said.
The Pentor survey of 3,000 households was held in the first half of this year.
